standard_prerequisites: Fields, Lemma lemma-separable-elements: the elements of an algebraic extension that are separable over the base form an intermediate field

Fields, Lemma lemma-irreducible-polynomials: for an algebraic element in positive characteristic there is a p-power q such that the minimal polynomial has the form P(x^q) with P separable; equivalently a suitable q-th power of the element is separable over the base
Purely inseparable extension: an algebraic extension in which every element has a minimal polynomial of the form x minus a q-th power of an element of the base, for some p-power q
core_obligations: In characteristic zero set E-sep equal to E; the tower exists trivially since every algebraic extension in characteristic zero is separable

Assume characteristic p greater than zero and let E-sep be the set of elements of E separable over F; by the separable-elements lemma this is an intermediate field, and by construction E-sep over F is separable

Given alpha in E, take the p-power q such that the minimal polynomial of alpha has the form P(x^q) with P separable; then alpha to the q is separable over F, so it lies in E-sep, and alpha is purely inseparable over E-sep; hence E over E-sep is purely inseparable

Uniqueness: any subextension F inside E-zero inside E with E-zero over F separable consists of separable elements, so E-zero is contained in E-sep; and any subextension over which E is purely inseparable must contain every separable element, so E-sep is contained in it; hence E-sep is the unique intermediate field with both properties
proof_roadmap: Handle characteristic zero trivially and define E-sep as the separable element field in characteristic p
Prove E over E-sep is purely inseparable via the q-th power trick on minimal polynomials
Argue uniqueness from the defining properties of the two classes of extensions
